# Inputs of atan's core reached through atan2, for atan2 (a function of two arguments): one
# pair a line, `y x`, each as its raw bits in hex (Double.doubleToRawLongBits), y first because
# it is atan2's first argument, which the harness calls its first. Read by
# Inputs.hardCasePairs("atan2"). Lines starting with # are comments.
#
# These are NOT hard-to-round cases of atan2, and V. Lefevre's file has none: its tags (em1 l1p
# log isr isq exp ash sh ch l10 ach th atn tan e10 asn sin cos acs ath ex2 lg2 e01 cub cbr in
# the copy of 21 November 2026) are all functions of one argument, so there is no atan2 tag to
# extract. What the file has is `atn`, the inputs t at which the exact atan(t) lies unusually
# close to a rounding boundary of binary64. e_atan2.c computes atan(fabs(y/x)) for the general
# lane and atan(y) when x is 1.0, so the pair (y, x) with |y/x| = t exactly sends t, such an
# input, into atan's core through atan2's own division, its checks on the high words and its
# quadrant code. For a port that follows fdlibm's operations exactly these are no harder than
# any other pair; their use is that a dropped correction term or a reassociated sum in the
# core, a change far below one ulp, is most likely to flip the result exactly at these points.
# The quadrants 2 and 3 of e_atan2.c compute pi - (z - pi_lo) and (z - pi_lo) - pi, which fdlibm
# does not round correctly, so at those pairs StrictMath's value is the oracle's and nothing
# else is claimed of it.
#
# Derivation, by dev/testlibm-extract.py (python3 -I dev/testlibm-extract.py atn atan2
# testlibm-data.xz), which is reproducible: the output equals this file's lines
# that start with 0x, in order. Source: V. Lefevre, hard-to-round cases in round-to-nearest, file
# testlibm-data (updated 2020-11-27), https://www.vinc17.net/research/testlibm/testlibm-data.xz,
# from the page https://www.vinc17.net/research/testlibm/, which states no licence or reuse
# terms: only the input values are taken, as numeric facts. Every line for "atn" in mode N is
# rechecked as for atan itself (the input is a double, the file's result is atan(t) rounded to
# nearest, and the direction bit is the 54th bit of the exact value, in 400-digit decimal
# arithmetic), and its |t| is taken once, in the file's order. For each |t| and for j in 0, 1,
# -5 the extractor prints x = +2^j, then -2^j, and for each x y = +|t| * 2^j, then -|t| * 2^j:
# 12 pairs, 4 quadrants at each of the three scales. A pair is kept only if |t| * 2^j is an
# exact normal double and |y/x| is exactly |t| in 400-digit arithmetic; none was dropped.
# j = 0 has x = +1.0, which is atan2's `x == 1.0` lane (atan(y) itself, with the sign of y),
# and x = -1.0, which is not.
#
# Measured by the same run: 1735 lines of mode N for atn, 1735 distinct |t| and none negative,
# so 20820 pairs, 0 dropped, 0 problems.
# arity: 2
